clue.text: Poet, reborn, burst out

indicators.note: 'burst out' reads as breaking loose, so the letters of the two words are freed into a new order

explanation.surface: A poet bursts out of his shell, born again.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns is Scotland's national bard, the writer of Auld Lang Syne, so a poet by example.

clue.text: Drink port

definitions.meaning: a whisky distilled mainly from ... grain
a town in East Sussex, one of the old Cinque Ports

explanation.surface: Drink some port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine, but it is the harbour town of Rye in East Sussex, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a whiskey made from rye grain, and also an ancient Sussex harbour town.

clue.text: In a taxi, one's upset by standard

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards
In puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
one is I, and the 's is is

explanation.surface: Someone in a taxi is upset by the norm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns everything round at the end: the whole run is read upwards, as in a down clue, giving the standard sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means fundamental or standard, the plain version without extras.

clue.text: Story of ancient church

parts.note: Roman suggests the ancient world of Rome
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A tale of an old church.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a story, originally a medieval tale of chivalry and adventure.

clue.text: Comedian in desert losing leader in movement

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other
losing its leader means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: to desert is to abandon
a wag is a joker or comedian

explanation.surface: A comedian in the desert drops out of the leading spot in a movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a noun, but it is the verb abandon; 'losing leader' leaves BANDON, and 'in' puts WAG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandwagon is a popular trend or movement that many people hurry to join.

clue.text: Sail with two men

parts.note: Roy is a man's name
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: Going sailing with a couple of chaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal is a small sail set above the topgallant on a square-rigged ship.

clue.text: Without hesitation, cooking cucumbers die from them?

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are worked over and rearranged
without means lacking, so those letters are removed

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Cooked cucumbers, eaten without a pause, might be fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes ER from CUCUMBERS to leave CUCUMBS, which 'cooking' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To succumb is to give way, especially to die from an illness or injury.

clue.text: Part of a gun producing smoke

indicators.note: 'Part of' says the wanted letters are a piece of the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: A component of a firearm that gives off smoke when fired.
explanation.walkthrough: The run lies across 'of a gun'; 'Part of' can't be read as just 'a gun', since its part comes from all three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Fag is British slang for a cigarette, the thing you smoke.

clue.text: Chinese money accepted by European for spice-producing plant

parts.note: the fen is a small Chinese coin, a hundredth of a yuan
U, as in U and non-U, means socially acceptable
a Greek is a European

explanation.surface: Chinese currency taken by someone in Europe to buy a spice plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U' is an old British label for upper-class usage, hence acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenugreek is a plant of the pea family whose seeds are ground as a spice in curries.

clue.text: People of varying ages provide Kelly with food

parts.note: Gene Kelly was the American dancer and film star
rations are allowances of food

explanation.surface: Providing someone named Kelly with something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Generations are groups of people born around the same time, so each of a different age.

clue.text: Can one get this for jam? Yes, one may exchange it

definitions.text: Can one get this for jam?

indicators.note: to exchange the letters is to swap their positions round, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A question about whether you can get something for jam, with an encouraging answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' is British slang for something easily come by (money for jam), so the question defines cash got without effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Money for jam is a British idiom for cash earned with no effort, the same idea as money won easily.

clue.text: Part of chapter in a set of books

definitions.meaning: a cathedral chapter is made up of clergy, each of these members holding the title
the accepted body of scripture or of an author's genuine works

explanation.surface: A section of a chapter within a series of volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a member of a cathedral chapter, and also the accepted list of sacred or authentic writings.

clue.text: Place showing prosperity these days, although having trouble in 1857

parts.note: good fortune or luck brings prosperity
these days means now, at present

explanation.surface: A town doing well today, though it had trouble long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail 'although having trouble in 1857' recalls the Siege of Lucknow in the Indian Mutiny; it adds colour to the definition rather than letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucknow is a city in northern India, capital of Uttar Pradesh, so it is a place.

clue.text: Marches men to well — it has been moved

indicators.note: something moved has been shifted about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A procession of men to a well that has been relocated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marches' looks like a verb or parade, but it is the surname of the four sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The March sisters, Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy, are the heroines of Alcott's novel of that title.

clue.text: Couch, having been extended, accommodates you, finally

indicators.note: to accommodate a guest is to take them in, so one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: something extended has been made longer

indicators.note: 'finally' points to the closing letter of the word you

explanation.surface: A sofa that has been lengthened, finally having room for you.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounger is a long reclining seat or couch for lazing about on.

clue.text: Pinch a piece of harness

definitions.meaning: a pinch is a tiny quantity, a mere hint of something
one of the two straps by which a horse pulls a cart

explanation.surface: Squeezing part of a horse's tack.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace is a minute amount, like a pinch, and also a side strap joining a draught horse's collar to the vehicle.

clue.text: A doctor given two sovereigns and one shilling for a perfume ingredient

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a monarch's cipher
GR, Georgius Rex, is another monarch's cipher
I is the Roman numeral one
s is the abbreviation for shilling, an old British coin

explanation.surface: A doctor is handed a couple of gold coins and a shilling to buy a scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereigns' look like gold coins but are the royal ciphers ER and GR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy substance from sperm whales used to fix scents in perfumery.

clue.text: Food, worst I scoffed, and most unhygienic

parts.note: grub is informal for food

indicators.note: to scoff is to eat greedily, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: to worst someone is to beat them, so to best them

explanation.surface: Food that is the worst I've ever wolfed down, and the dirtiest too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worst' looks like an adjective but is the verb meaning defeat; 'scoffed' puts I inside BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Grubby means dirty, so the superlative means the most unclean or unhygienic.

clue.text: Cover up furniture in court case

parts.note: to be up before the judge is to be in court
a holster is a case for a pistol

explanation.surface: Concealing furniture during a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster is to fit chairs and sofas with padding and a fabric covering.

clue.text: Heading north by rail, convoluted and perplexing route

indicators.note: convoluted means twisted and tangled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Nth is a standard abbreviation of north

explanation.surface: Travelling north by train on a tangled, confusing route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading' only sets the scene as a direction of travel; NTH with BYRAIL is rearranged by 'convoluted'.
explanation.definitionFit: A labyrinth is a maze, a winding and bewildering path that is hard to find your way through.

clue.text: This will produce a reaction regarding a man…

parts.note: re means regarding, about
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: Something that will get a response concerning a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance added in chemistry to bring about a reaction.

clue.text: This covers an Asian city, as well as covering a state

indicators.note: covering means one piece lies over and around the other

parts.note: as well means too, also
KY is the postal abbreviation of Kentucky, a US state

explanation.surface: A clue playing on the word covering: something that covers a city and a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo is the capital of Japan, a city in Asia.

clue.text: … an acrobat used to drink

explanation.surface: An acrobat who used to drink, continuing the man from the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler is an acrobat doing somersaults, and also a straight-sided drinking glass.

clue.text: Pronunciation of two rivers causes conflict

indicators.note: pronunciation means the words are spoken, so their sound gives the entry

parts.note: the Wharfe is a Yorkshire river and the Ayr a Scottish one

explanation.surface: How you say the names of two rivers leads to a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wharfe runs through Yorkshire in England and the Ayr through Ayrshire in Scotland; said together they sound like the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Warfare is armed fighting between nations or groups, so conflict.

clue.text: Half-heartedly shake up the jo

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Half-heartedly shake up the jo (5)' is cut short at 'jo' (likely 'joint'); the fodder and the rest are missing, the scan does not show it, and a search found nothing.

clue.text: Stories about cat in French city

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: stories are fibs or lies
mog is British slang for a cat

explanation.surface: Tales about a cat set in a city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Limoges is a city in west-central France, famous for its porcelain.

clue.text: Two family members of great distinction

parts.note: gran is a grandmother
d is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A couple of relatives who are very distinguished.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand means imposing and distinguished, of high rank or great importance.

clue.text: Endeavour to reveal the code

definitions.meaning: Endeavour is the first name of Inspector ..., the Oxford detective of the books and TV series
the telegraphic code of dots and dashes

explanation.surface: Trying hard to crack the code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endeavour' looks like a verb meaning try, but it is the rarely used first name of Colin Dexter's detective Inspector Morse.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Endeavour Morse shares his surname with the inventor of the dot-and-dash telegraph code.

clue.text: Formidable female cricketer, English, overwhelmed by praise upon retirement

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket

indicators.note: to be overwhelmed by something is to be engulfed in it, so one piece sits inside the other
retirement means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to exalt is to praise highly

explanation.surface: A fearsome woman cricketer, an Englishwoman, swamped with tributes when she retires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upon retirement' reverses the word for praise, giving TLAXE. 'overwhelmed by' puts the E for English inside that, after the cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: A battleaxe is a domineering, aggressive older woman, so a formidable female.

clue.text: Watch the way he finishes

indicators.note: the finishes of the words are their closing letters

explanation.surface: Observe how he ends things.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to watch it closely.

clue.text: Letters from abroad newspaper rejected

indicators.note: rejected suggests being thrown back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: Foreign letters turned down by a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters from abroad' sounds like foreign correspondence, but means letters of a foreign alphabet: nu is the Greek N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, so its plural is a set of foreign letters.

clue.text: Crossing over river to make tea around hilltop

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to brew is to make tea
a ridge is the long crest of a hill

explanation.surface: Instructions to brew tea on a hill while crossing a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the tea-making verb back to front, giving WERB. The definition is 'Crossing over river' because this London bridge spans the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Tower Bridge carries traffic over the Thames in London, a crossing over a river.
